        /// <summary>
        /// Adds this assembly's generated validators, and a validation runner for each
        /// validated type.
        ///
        /// Not idempotent. Calling this twice registers every validator twice, and a
        /// runner merges every registered validator for a type - so each error would be
        /// reported twice. Add rather than TryAdd is deliberate: registering a second
        /// validator for one type is how a hand-written rule composes with the generated
        /// one, so this cannot dedupe without breaking that.
        /// </summary>

        {

            global::Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.ServiceCollectionServiceExtensions.AddSingleton<global::ValidationModules.IValidatorFor<global::Sample.Owner>, global::Sample.OwnerValidator>(services);

            global::Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.ServiceCollectionServiceExtensions.AddSingleton<global::ValidationModules.IDynamicValidator, global::Sample.DogDynamicValidator>(services);
            global::Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.ServiceCollectionServiceExtensions.AddSingleton<global::ValidationModules.IDynamicValidator, global::Sample.OwnerDynamicValidator>(services);

            // TryAdd and a factory: every assembly's registration wants the same registry,
            // built once over whatever adapters all of them contributed. A factory rather
            // than a type so nothing is constructed reflectively under Native AOT.
            global::Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.Extensions.ServiceCollectionDescriptorExtensions.TryAddSingleton(services, provider => new global::ValidationModules.DynamicValidatorRegistry(global::Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.ServiceProviderServiceExtensions.GetServices<global::ValidationModules.IDynamicValidator>(provider)));

            global::Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.ValidationModulesServiceCollectionExtensions.AddValidationRunner<global::Sample.Dog>(services);
            global::Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.ValidationModulesServiceCollectionExtensions.AddValidationRunner<global::Sample.Owner>(services);

            // Element-wise validation for collection bodies - List<T> and T[] - so a batch
            // endpoint's .Validate<List<T>>() resolves a validator that walks the elements
            // with indexed paths. Closed per type, for the AOT reason above.
